confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including references and both supplementary texts, and checked the form's numbers against the PDF. The on-file PDF has 23 pages and is explicitly marked arXiv:2411.03827v1 [cs.HC], 6 Nov 2024; the title and four authors match the form (PDF p. 1, title, byline, and arXiv stamp).

One individual, between-subject laboratory randomized experiment: the Fig. 4 caption explicitly says participants were randomly divided between DesignMinds and usual design practice; the system ran locally in a lab and participants attended individually (PDF p. 8, Section 4.2; p. 9, Fig. 4 caption and Section 4.4.1). The lab_rct classification is supported.

The study recruited 35 people, described as BSc/MSc students or PhD candidates: 17 females, 18 males, mean age 25.4 years (PDF p. 8, Section 4.1). Fig. 4 labels the experimental group N=18 and control group N=17 (PDF p. 9). The creativity tests report 33 degrees of freedom (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1), and experimental-group correlations explicitly report n=18 (PDF p. 13, Section 5.2.2). No exclusions or separate larger recruitment/assignment count are reported; the form appropriately states that the tests are consistent with all 35 analyzed.
The independent community of 30 designers selected six design books for the knowledge repository; these are not additional participants in the randomized ideation experiment (PDF p. 5, Section 3).
The prototype uses blip2-opt-6.7b, GPT-4 API gpt-4-0125-preview, text-embedding-ada-002, LlamaIndex, and Gradio, with six design books used for retrieval augmentation (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 3).

Participants completed two ideation tasks using cooking and construction videos from Ego4D, approximately 3 minutes each, with counterbalanced order and a maximum of 15 minutes per video. DesignMinds was available during experimental-group ideation; the chatbot was hidden for controls (PDF p. 10, Section 4.4.1; p. 23, Supplementary Text 1).

Three independent raters evaluated the produced ideation texts for fluency, flexibility, and originality. Originality used a 7-point Likert scale; fluency counted comprehensive ideas and flexibility assessed domains/subdomains covered (PDF p. 8, Section 4.3.1; p. 11, Section 5.1; p. 23, Supplementary Text 2). These are output-scored with_ai outcomes; flexibility is not a reported between-person homogenization measure.

Originality matches exactly: experimental 4.74 ? 1.018 points, control 3.35 ? 0.583 points; independent t-test t(33)=4.674, p<.001 (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1). The printed ? quantities are retained without assigning them an unsupported SD or SE label.
Flexibility matches exactly: experimental 7.17 ? 3.511 points, control 5.12 ? 1.074 points; independent t-test t(33)=2.304, p=.014 (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1).

Fluency matches exactly: independent t-test t(33)=1.885, p=.068, described as not significant. Arm means are plotted without exact numeric labels in the radar chart; the form does not estimate them (PDF p. 10, Fig. 5; p. 11, Section 5.1). All statistics and directions in the one-line finding match these passages.

Supplementary Texts 1 and 2 are included on PDF p. 23 and contain task instructions and rating criteria, with no additional outcome estimates. The paper is an experiment, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates to verify.

Random assignment and output-scored creativity are present, but the study sample is below 50 people. Thus core=no and context_class=none agree with the codebook; has_randomized_people_study=true requires the two-screener pipeline despite the small sample (PDF pp. 8-11, Sections 4.1, 4.4.1 and 5.1, and Fig. 4).
summary: The form's design and context classifications, participant counts, source version, and reported creativity statistics agree with the on-file arXiv v1. This randomized laboratory study includes 35 people (18 DesignMinds, 17 control), so it belongs in the two-screener pipeline but falls below the 50-person core threshold.
